tagline: See what each pull request really changed before you merge it
use_when: Pull requests are waiting, especially ones an AI agent opened while you were away, and you want screenshots and findings instead of reading a diff.
try_it: Use the pr-qa skill to check every open pull request before I merge anything.

features.label: Every Open PR, Every Time
features.sub: With no arguments, it checks all open pull requests
features.title: With no arguments, it checks all open pull requests
features.what: The list comes from your code host, not from whatever the conversation happened to mention. It says up front which pull requests it is covering, and names any it skipped and why.
features.html:
3 open: #12, #15, #16
Checking all 3.
skipped: none

features.label: Nothing Goes Quiet
features.sub: An opt-in start-of-session note says how many PRs are open
features.title: Each new session says how many PRs are open
features.what: Turn on the optional session reminder with one command and each new session starts with a short note saying how many pull requests are open and how old the oldest one is. It ships with the plugin but stays off until you turn it on with one setting in your project's settings file, and then stays silent when there is no token, no network or nothing open. A pull request nobody mentioned cannot sit unreviewed for days.
features.html:
New session
2 pull requests open.
Oldest: 3 days.

features.label: Runs It for Real
features.sub: Each branch is checked out, started and used
features.title: Each branch is checked out, started and used
features.what: Every pull request is read first to find the page and the record that show the change, then run for real: checked out, started up, signed in and photographed. Helper scripts pick the pages from a map you write for your own routes, and you bring the screenshot step (the scripts read the before and after evidence you produce). Nothing is recommended for merging that was not actually run.
features.html: diff read branch checked out app started signed in after shots taken

features.label: Before Shots Come First
features.sub: The main branch is photographed before anything changes
features.title: The main branch is photographed before anything changes
features.what: Before pictures are taken on the main branch before the pull request runs, so a database change cannot get in the way of capturing the old state.
features.html:
1 · mainbefore shots
2 · branchafter shots

features.label: Desktop and Phone, Every PR
features.sub: Both screen sizes for every pull request
features.title: Both screen sizes for every pull request
features.what: Every pull request is captured at desktop size and at phone size, even a change that seems desktop-only, because phone layouts are where things quietly break.

features.label: Proof It Signed In
features.sub: It refuses to save a picture of the sign-in page
features.title: It refuses to save a picture of the sign-in page
features.what: Before any screenshot is saved, it checks the page is not the sign-in form and that something unique to the change is on screen. A failed sign-in can look like a normal page load, and four perfect pictures of a login form are not evidence.

features.label: Real People Stay Private
features.sub: Names and emails are replaced before the shot
features.title: Names and emails are replaced before the shot
features.what: On admin pages, real names and email addresses are overwritten on the page before the screenshot is taken, so nothing personal reaches the shared review page. Cropping afterward is not trusted to do the same job. Your screenshot step is told to do this redaction.

features.label: Its Own Tests, Counted
features.sub: Says whether the pull request added any tests
features.title: Says whether the pull request added any tests
features.what: The pull request's own tests are run, and the report says whether it added any. A passing suite and a tested change are not the same claim.
features.html:
48 tests pass
Tests added by this PR0

features.label: What Tests Can’t Catch
features.sub: A checklist of problems that pass every test
features.title: A checklist of problems that pass every test
features.what: Each pull request is checked for things a green suite misses: two PRs making the same database change, old records missing new data, layouts that wrap badly, private details showing up where they shouldn't, a page left outside a lock, and comments that contradict the code.

features.label: Honest When It Can’t Reproduce
features.sub: Says so when the reported bug doesn't happen
features.title: Says so when the reported bug doesn't happen
features.what: If the original bug cannot be made to happen, the report says so instead of calling the change a confirmed fix. It may still be an improvement, but you learn to check it on a real device.
features.html:

features.label: No Useless Pictures
features.sub: Common setup mistakes are ruled out first
features.title: Common setup mistakes are ruled out first
features.what: Before shooting, it rules out the usual ways a screenshot run goes wrong: missing styles, missing settings, two apps on one port, and a sample record that doesn't show the change. Every picture is looked at before it goes on the page.
features.html: styles built settings in place free port record shows the change every shot looked at

features.label: The Verdict Up Top
features.sub: A summary table you can decide from alone
features.title: A summary table you can decide from alone
features.what: The page opens with a table of every pull request: its test result and the recommended action. You can stop reading there and still make a decision.

features.label: Worst First
features.sub: The one that must not merge sits at the top
features.title: The one that must not merge sits at the top
features.what: Pull requests are ordered worst first, each with a status label, so bad news is never buried under the safe ones.

features.label: Flip Between Views
features.sub: Before/After and Desktop/Phone switches on each PR
features.title: Before/After and Desktop/Phone switches on each PR
features.what: Each pull request has two switches, Before/After and Desktop/Phone, over a single picture. It opens on the view that shows the change best.
features.html: BeforeAfterDesktopPhone

features.label: Phone at Phone Size
features.sub: Phone shots are shown at true phone width
features.title: Phone shots are shown at true phone width
features.what: Phone screenshots are shown at real phone width and centered, not stretched across the card, where giant text would make them look like desktop shots. They are captured sharp enough to stay crisp at that size.

features.label: Findings in Plain Words
features.sub: Numbered findings: what is wrong and why it matters
features.title: Numbered findings: what is wrong and why it matters
features.what: Each finding is one sentence on what is wrong and one on why it matters. You can act on them, or send them back as the brief for another try.

features.label: Unchecked Never Looks Clean
features.sub: A PR nobody reviewed says so plainly
features.title: A PR nobody reviewed says so plainly
features.what: If no reviewer has written findings for a pull request, it reads “not yet read by a reviewer” instead of showing an empty, problem-free list. A gap stays visible as a gap.

features.label: Tested Before You See It
features.sub: The review page is checked before it's published
features.title: The review page is checked before it's published
features.what: Before publishing, the page is loaded and clicked through automatically: every picture is present, the switches change the picture, phone view stays phone-sized, and the export lists every pull request.

features.label: Four Clear Choices
features.sub: Merge and push, merge and hold, send back, or wait
features.title: Merge and push, merge and hold, send back, or wait
features.what: Each pull request gets one decision, with a line under each option saying exactly what will happen. Wait, I will check it myself is always there, because not deciding yet is allowed.
features.html:
Merge and pushMerge, hold the push
Send it backWait, I'll check it

features.label: A Recommendation, Not a Default
features.sub: The suggested choice is marked, never pre-selected
features.title: The suggested choice is marked, never pre-selected
features.what: The recommended decision carries a badge, but nothing is selected for you. Nobody can approve a merge by scrolling past it, and an untouched pull request exports as no decision yet.

features.sub: Copy my decisions sends every verdict to Claude
features.title: Copy my decisions sends every verdict to Claude
features.what: One button copies a plain-text block per pull request, which you paste into chat to have the decisions carried out.

features.label: Done the Way You Said
features.sub: Each decision is carried out, one per pull request
features.title: Each decision is carried out, one per pull request
features.what: Merges are made, held locally or pushed exactly as chosen, with a note when a deploy or database change follows. Sent-back findings become the brief for another attempt, and if that needs you to edit a ticket, it tells you instead of quietly doing the work itself.
features.html:

#15 send back→ findings = new brief

features.label: Leaves No Mess
features.sub: Your project is put back the way it was
features.title: Your project is put back the way it was
features.what: When it is done, test database changes are rolled back, the main branch is checked out again, and temporary working copies are removed, because other sessions may be using the same machine.
features.html: database changes rolled back main checked out temporary copies removed

features.label: Where the Page Goes
features.sub: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.title: A private link, a local file, or your Wi-Fi
features.what: Your project picks where review pages go: a private claude.ai link, an HTML file that opens in your browser, or that file served on your home Wi-Fi so a phone can open it. Nothing is ever uploaded or tunneled in the Wi-Fi mode, and the server stops when the review ends.
